name: invoke-agent-action
description: Spawn a child agent when a lifecycle event fires — e.g. a coder's Stop hook spawns a code-reviewer. Bounded by a recursion-depth cap, a concurrency cap, and the subagent approval gate; always fire-and-forget so the lifecycle never blocks. Attach to an agent to activate.
author: PersonalClaw

x-meta.label: Task
x-meta.help: Prompt for the spawned agent. Supports $EVENT, $CONTEXT, and $<payload-key>.

x-meta.label: Agent
x-meta.help: Child agent name (e.g. code-reviewer). Empty uses the default agent.

x-meta.label: Working folder
x-meta.help: The folder the agent works in, so its file tools reach the files there, e.g. ~/Documents. The workspace, or a folder listed in Settings → Agent defaults → Allowed working directories. Empty uses the workspace. In a folder you haven't trusted, its agent only reads, whatever its Capability, until you trust the folder.

x-meta.label: Files it may change
x-meta.help: The files or folders this automation's job changes, each a full path (from / or ~/): its agent may write to these and to nothing else, and every other change and every command stay refused. Allowing the automation says so. Leave it empty for an automation that only reads. Not for an agent that runs on an agent CLI: PersonalClaw can't limit a CLI's own file edits to them.

x-meta.label: Max Turns
x-meta.help: Optional turn cap for the child agent.

x-meta.label: Model
x-meta.help: Optional model override for the child agent.

x-meta.label: Approval
x-meta.help: Set 'auto' to let its agent approve every tool call it makes without asking you (read-only unless Capability is mutating). Empty: its agent asks you before each call that needs approval, unless Settings → Agent defaults → Approval mode is Auto.

x-meta.label: Capability
x-meta.help: Read-only by default: an auto-fired child agent gets read/search tools only, and write/execute is denied. Set 'mutating' to grant this hook write and execute tools (the creation-time write grant), which it gets in a Working folder only once you trust that folder.
